title: Tachyon configuration (tachyon.yml)
description: Declares the agents and settings Tachyon orchestrates in this workspace.

agents.description: Agents (AI CLIs, dev servers, watchers — any command) keyed by name.

cmd.description: Shell command that runs the agent.

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to the workspace root or absolute.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the agent's session.

autostart.description: Start this agent when Tachyon starts.

watch.description: Glob(s) — restart the agent when a matching file changes.

restart.description: Crash policy: on-crash auto-restarts when the process dies with a non-zero exit (backoff 2s/4s/8s, max 3 per minute). Clean exits (0) never auto-restart.

attention.description: Needs-you detection. Defaults: on for kind=agent, off for kind=terminal. Object form tunes the idle threshold and adds prompt patterns.

silenceSec.description: Seconds of unchanged pane + idle CPU before the agent is marked idle.

patterns.description: Extra prompt regexes (case-insensitive) that mark the agent as needing input.

kind.description: agent = AI CLI (claude, codex, ...); terminal = server/shell/build. Default: inferred from cmd. Drives sidebar grouping and attention defaults.

instructions.description: Persistent operational specialization for this agent. Distinct from identity and the current execution task.

soul.description: Enable identity from the canonical Tachyon-owned .tachyon/agents/<agent>/SOUL.md profile. true enables; false or absence disables. Agents only.

role.description: Built-in role template (spec 216): a reusable task contract composed with 'instructions' at delivery (template first). agents-only; not valid for a terminal.

worktree.description: Run this agent in its own git worktree + branch (opt-in, off by default). Isolates parallel agents so they don't clobber each other's files.

branch.description: Literal branch name for this agent's worktree (overrides the global settings.worktree.branch template). Validated via git check-ref-format at creation.

worktreeSetup.description: Command(s) run ONCE in the fresh worktree before the agent starts (sequential, stop-on-failure). $TACHYON_WORKSPACE_ROOT and $TACHYON_WORKTREE_ROOT are set.

verify.description: Verify-gate (spec 214): a command/runbook name (or inline shell) run IN the worktree to prove it shippable. Resolves like a runbook step (command name > runbook name > inline). Advisory — surfaces a pass/fail/stale badge, never blocks.

harness.description: Isolated harness (spec 226/228/298/311 + grok/hermes): agent-scoped MCP, skills, runtime-native instructions/rules, and hooks materialized into a private config home so they never leak to sibling agents. Supported: claude, codex, opencode, grok, hermes (a harness on another runtime/terminal entry is a config error). Claude supports rules/skills/hooks/MCP; Codex supports instructions/skills/hooks/MCP; OpenCode/Grok/Hermes support mcp/skills/hooks (and empty harness:{} for private home + Bridge). Tachyon owns the config home + MCP plumbing — do not set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME, GROK_HOME, HERMES_HOME, or XDG_*_HOME in env. NOTE: cross-field rules are enforced by the loadConfig validator (not expressible in pure JSON Schema).

inherit.description: Whether to seed the workspace base before overlaying. 'none' = clean slate (sees ONLY the declared config); 'workspace' = the workspace .mcp.json snapshot plus the declared servers. 'global' is a follow pass (not yet supported). Default: workspace.

mcp.description: MCP servers scoped to THIS agent only (stdio shape). Each env value must be an exact ${VAR} reference — never a literal — so no secret is written to disk; claude expands it from the agent's process env at spawn.

hooks.description: spec 228/311 — runtime-native hooks. Claude: settings.json hooks object. Codex: hooks.<Event> config.toml object. Runtime validates the detailed event schema.

rules.description: spec 228 — Claude-only rule file path(s), concatenated into the agent's private CLAUDE.md (its own behavioral context). Workspace-relative; a single string or a non-empty list. Codex uses instructions instead.

instructions.description: spec 311 — Codex-only instruction file path(s), concatenated into the agent's private CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md. Workspace-relative; a single string or a non-empty list.

skills.description: spec 228/311 — skill dir path(s) (each holding a SKILL.md), copied into the agent's private skills/ directory. Workspace-relative; a single string or a non-empty list.

terminals.description: Terminals (servers, shells, builds) keyed by name (spec 215). Same entry shape as an agent, but kind is always 'terminal' (so 'kind' and 'instructions' aren't meaningful here — loadConfig rejects them) and attention defaults off. The engine treats these identically to an agents: entry with kind: terminal — this block just reads more naturally.

layouts.description: Deprecated — the named-layouts feature was retired (use VS Code's native editor groups). This block is accepted for backward compatibility but ignored.

maxAgents.description: Max concurrently running agents in this workspace (fork-bomb guardrail). Overrides the tachyon.maxAgents editor setting.

bridgePort.description: Fixed port for the Bridge MCP server. Default: a stable per-workspace port derived from the workspace path (41000-42999) — registrations survive editor restarts either way.

auth.description: Require a Bearer token on every Bridge call (default true). The stable per-workspace token lives in extension storage and is injected as TACHYON_BRIDGE_TOKEN into every agent Tachyon spawns; registered configs reference the env var, so no secret lands in committable files.

legacyBridgeAuth.description: Accept the shared/legacy Bridge token as a caller identity (spec 351). Default true for existing workspaces during the per-agent-token migration window; every legacy-authenticated call is logged and cannot claim a currently-live agent's identity. Set false once every runtime you use has switched to per-agent tokens (TACHYON_AGENT_BRIDGE_TOKEN).

layout.description: Deprecated — the named-layouts feature was retired. Accepted for backward compatibility but ignored.

tmux.description: tmux server options applied to Tachyon's dedicated socket as `set -g <key> <value>`. Tachyon's defaults (mouse on, focus-events on, history-limit 10000) apply first and this overlays them; 'remain-on-exit' is reserved (crash detection depends on it). Your ~/.tmux.conf is never loaded. Values may be booleans (on/off), numbers, or strings.

base.description: Location root for worktrees; path = <base>/<wsHash>/<agent>. Default ~/.cache/tachyon/worktrees (XDG-aware).

branch.description: Global branch-name template; MUST contain {agent}. Default tachyon/{agent}.

verify.description: Global default verify-gate (spec 214) for worktree agents that don't declare their own. A command/runbook name or inline shell; a per-agent verify wins.
Project-owned commands and optional named-behavior adapter used by verify_task. Tachyon supplies no package-manager, runner, or test-location defaults.

full.description: Full verification argv command. Required when verify_task is called with full=true.

typecheck.description: Optional typecheck argv command run before behavior verification.

prepare.description: Optional project-owned argv command that provisions dependencies independently in every isolated BASE/HEAD clone; required when behavior is configured.

affected.description: Optional affected-test argv prefix; Tachyon appends existing changed paths as option-safe relative arguments.

behavior.description: Explicit opt-in adapter for plain behavior-test identifiers. The named oracle must already be project-owned and tracked; cmd: verifiers bypass this adapter.

adapter.description: Named-test mechanics selected by the project; never inferred by Tachyon.

command.description: Argv prefix. The vitest-name adapter appends --run -t <identifier> --reporter=json.

stubPath.description: POSIX workspace-relative path template containing {agent} for a pre-existing tracked fixed oracle; runtime validation also rejects control characters and unsafe segments.

executorPaths.description: Tracked project files that define verifier execution (manifest, lockfile, runner/config inputs). Their committed hashes are fixed at spawn and must match BASE and HEAD.

auto.description: Auto re-inject an agent's role reminder after a detected compaction (claude/codex only), on the next idle window. OFF by default — it types into the live terminal. The manual 'Re-anchor agent' command and .tachyon/ROLE.md work regardless.

bridgeGuidance.description: Append Bridge-coordination guidance to agents spawned via the Bridge so delegated work stays visible in Tachyon (spec 216). Default true.

projectGuidance.description: Opt-in, project-owned agent guidance loaded from explicitly declared source-workspace files. Tachyon transports the files in order and does not discover runtime-specific context files.

files.description: Ordered, non-empty list of unique workspace-relative guidance files. Runtime validation additionally enforces UTF-8 byte, containment, file-type and aggregate-content limits.

clipboard.description: Clean clipboard copy (spec 219). 'auto' wires a UTF-8 copy-mode helper so a plain mouse drag-select (incl. scrollback) copies clean — no Shift, mouse stays on. 'off' leaves the OSC 52 default (use if copy already works or on a headless box).

taskNotifications.description: Shared defaults for VS Code task mutation notifications. Explicit user and workspace editor settings take precedence.

gitDelivery.description: GitDelivery lifecycle and hygiene settings (spec 365). Profiles supply defaults; explicit keys override profile values.

autoOpen.description: Open a local GitDelivery record automatically when an ad-hoc worktree agent successfully spawns.

requireNonSelfAccept.description: Strict-profile review gate knob reserved for Phase 2 integrate behavior.

autoPrune.description: Reserved for Phase 2; Phase 1 never auto-prunes.

prunePrincipals.description: Agent principals allowed to prune deliveries they do not own.

delivery.description: Canonical Delivery rollout settings (spec 368). Legacy gated persistence remains the default.

commands.description: One-shot commands (test, lint, migrate...): run -> exit -> show result. Unlike agents/terminals, exiting is expected (exit 0 = pass). Agents can run them via the curated run_command tool.

cmd.description: Shell command; its exit code is the result.

cwd.description: Working directory (relative to workspace root or absolute).

runbooks.description: Step-by-step procedures composed of commands. Steps run sequentially in their own sessions; a non-zero exit stops the runbook (the failed pane is kept). Steps are exact command-name references or inline shell strings.
